title: @supports and feature queries
learningObjectives: Explain @supports and feature queries and use modern CSS features responsibly.

understand.concept: The @supports at-rule applies CSS declarations only when the browser reports support for a specified property/value or selector condition. It enables progressive enhancement: provide a baseline style first, then add an enhanced style inside a feature query.
understand.whyItMatters: Feature queries help a page remain usable when newer CSS is unavailable. They detect CSS feature support, not whether a feature behaves correctly in every context or whether a user prefers a particular presentation.
understand.analogy: A feature query is like checking whether a tool is available before using it, while keeping a basic method ready.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS parsing, specificity, and feature support follow the relevant browser standards.

explain.narrative: The base style remains defined; browsers that support grid apply the enhancement.

questions.prompt: What is a good principle for maintainable modern CSS?
options: Use clear rules, appropriate fallbacks, and inspect computed behaviour
Use the newest feature everywhere without checking support
Increase specificity whenever a style does not apply
questions.answer: Use clear rules, appropriate fallbacks, and inspect computed behaviour
questions.explanation: Maintainability depends on clarity, support-aware enhancement, and understanding the cascade.
